problem:
The triangle $D$ has vertices $(0,0),(6,0),(2,5).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039564/assets/059560835586e9c149cdb5dabcddc80610a58bfa0c30cb5f685b8bb6bdca3e90.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 5=15.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=2\cdot 2-0\cdot 0=4.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,4\,|\cdot 15 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$
